title: Spec of a universal square-zero thickening of rings is a universal first order thickening of affine schemes
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $\pi:S'\to S$ be a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $K$ satisfies $K^2=0$ and which has the following universal property: for every $R$-algebra $A$, every ideal $I\subseteq A$ with $I^2=0$ (quotient map $q:A\to A/I$) and every $R$-algebra map $a:S\to A/I$, there is exactly one $R$-algebra map $a':S'\to A$ with $q\circ a'=a\circ\pi$. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$, $Z'=\operatorname{Spec}S'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $h=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:Z\to X$, $i=\operatorname{Spec}\pi:Z\to Z'$ and $h'=\operatorname{Spec}(R\to S'):Z'\to X$. Then $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] has square zero [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $h'\circ i=h$, and $Z\subset Z'$ (with $h'$) is a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]: the universal property holds for all first order thickenings $T\subset T'$ over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with $T'$ an arbitrary (not necessarily affine) scheme.

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), third paragraph ('Before we glue affine pieces ... Thus the lemma holds if X and Z are affine'): the universal property for affine T, T' from Algebra, Lemma 04EB, then for general T' by an affine open covering of T' and glueing of the morphisms

proof.text: *Notation and the dictionary of morphisms into spectra.* Write $\varphi':R\to S'$ for the structure map of the $R$-algebra $S'$; $\pi\circ\varphi'=\varphi$ since $\pi$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, and $h'=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi'$. For a scheme $Y$ write $\Gamma(Y)=\mathcal O_Y(Y)$, and for a morphism of schemes $g:Y_1\to Y_2$ write $g^*:\Gamma(Y_2)\to\Gamma(Y_1)$ for the ring map it induces on global sections; $(g\circ g')^*=g'^*\circ g^*$ and $\mathrm{id}^*=\mathrm{id}$, since morphisms of schemes compose as morphisms of locally ringed spaces [def-pc-scheme]. For a ring $B$ let $\varepsilon_B:B\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B)$ be the canonical isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], for every scheme $Y$ the map $\mu_Y:\operatorname{Mor}(Y,\operatorname{Spec}B)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Ring}}(B,\Gamma(Y))$, $f\mapsto f^*\circ\varepsilon_B$, is bijective. It has two compatibilities: (D1) for $g:Y_1\to Y_2$ and $f:Y_2\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\mu_{Y_1}(f\circ g)=g^*\circ f^*\circ\varepsilon_B=g^*\circ\mu_{Y_2}(f)$; (D2) for a ring map $\psi:C\to B$ and $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\mu_Y(\operatorname{Spec}\psi\circ f)=f^*\circ(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^*\circ\varepsilon_C=f^*\circ\varepsilon_B\circ\psi=\mu_Y(f)\circ\psi$, by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-global-sections] ($(\operatorname{Spec}\psi)^*\circ\varepsilon_C=\varepsilon_B\circ\psi$) [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

proof.text: *$Z\subset Z'$ is a first order thickening over $X$.* (a) $h'\circ i=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi'\circ\operatorname{Spec}\pi=\operatorname{Spec}(\pi\circ\varphi')=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=h$ by the functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. (b) $i$ is a closed immersion: cover $Z'$ by the single affine open $V=Z'$; then $i^{-1}(V)=Z=\operatorname{Spec}S$ is affine, and the ring map $i^*:\Gamma(Z')\to\Gamma(Z)$ is $\varepsilon_S\circ\pi\circ\varepsilon_{S'}^{-1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-map-global-sections], which is surjective because $\pi$ is. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (2), $i$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. (c) Its ideal sheaf $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_{Z'}\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] has $\mathcal I(Z')=\ker(i^*)=\varepsilon_{S'}(K)$. By [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], on the affine open $U=Z'$ one has $\mathcal I^2|_{Z'}=(\mathcal I(Z')\mathcal I(Z'))^\sim=(\varepsilon_{S'}(K^2))^\sim=0$ since $K^2=0$; as $U$ is all of $Z'$, $\mathcal I^2=0$. (d) By (b), (c) and [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (2), $Z'$ is a first order thickening of $Z$ via $i$, and by (a) and [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] (4) it is one over $X$ with structure morphism $h'$, $Z$ being over $X$ through $h=h'\circ i$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

proof.text: *The universal property when $T'$ is affine.* Let $T\subset T'$ be a first order thickening over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] with closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$, ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ ($\mathcal J^2=0$) and structure morphism $b:T'\to X$, with $T'$ affine, and let $a:T\to Z$ satisfy $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$. We show: there is exactly one $a':T'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ a'=b$ and $a'\circ i_T=i\circ a$. Put $A=\Gamma(T')$, $C=\Gamma(T)$. Since $T'$ is an affine open of itself and $i_T^{-1}(T')=T$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion] (1) shows that $i_T^*:A\to C$ is surjective. Its kernel is $N=\mathcal J(T')$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $N^2=0$ by [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers] ($\mathcal J^2=0$ means $\mathcal J(U)^2=0$ on every affine open $U$; take $U=T'$). Let $q:A\to A/N$ be the quotient map and $\bar\imath:A/N\to C$ the isomorphism with $\bar\imath\circ q=i_T^*$. Put $\beta=\mu_{T'}(b):R\to A$; this makes $A$ an $R$-algebra, and $A/N$ one via $q\circ\beta$. Put $\alpha=\mu_T(a):S\to C$ and $a_0=\bar\imath^{-1}\circ\alpha:S\to A/N$. By (D2) and (D1) of the first step, $\mu_T(h\circ a)=\alpha\circ\varphi$ and $\mu_T(b\circ i_T)=i_T^*\circ\beta$, so $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$ gives $\alpha\circ\varphi=i_T^*\circ\beta$, hence $a_0\circ\varphi=\bar\imath^{-1}\circ i_T^*\circ\beta=q\circ\beta$: $a_0$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. Now let $a':T'\to Z'$ be any morphism and $\alpha'=\mu_{T'}(a'):S'\to A$. (i) Since $\mu_{T'}$ is injective, $h'\circ a'=b$ iff $\mu_{T'}(h'\circ a')=\beta$, i.e. by (D2) iff $\alpha'\circ\varphi'=\beta$, i.e. iff $\alpha'$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras. (ii) Since $\mu_T$ is injective, $a'\circ i_T=i\circ a$ iff $\mu_T(a'\circ i_T)=\mu_T(i\circ a)$, i.e. by (D1), (D2) iff $i_T^*\circ\alpha'=\alpha\circ\pi$, i.e. (applying the isomorphism $\bar\imath^{-1}$) iff $q\circ\alpha'=a_0\circ\pi$. Since $\mu_{T'}:\operatorname{Mor}(T',Z')\to\operatorname{Hom}(S',A)$ is bijective, the $a'$ with both properties correspond bijectively to the $R$-algebra maps $\alpha':S'\to A$ with $q\circ\alpha'=a_0\circ\pi$. By the universal property of $\pi$ in the hypothesis, applied to the $R$-algebra $A$, the ideal $N$ ($N^2=0$) and the $R$-algebra map $a_0:S\to A/N$, there is exactly one such $\alpha'$. Hence exactly one $a'$. (Only $T'$ affine is used: $T$ is then affine as well, but this is not needed.)

proof.text: *Restriction to opens.* Keep $T\subset T'$, $i_T$, $b$, $a$ as in the universal property for an arbitrary scheme $T'$. For an open subscheme $U'\subseteq T'$ with inclusion $j_{U'}$ [def-weil-open-immersion] let $U=i_T^{-1}(U')$ with inclusion $j_U$ and $i_U:U\to U'$ the unique morphism with $j_{U'}\circ i_U=i_T\circ j_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. By [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-open-restriction] (applied with the open $X\subseteq X$), $U\subset U'$ via $i_U$ is a first order thickening over $X$ with structure morphism $b\circ j_{U'}$, and $a\circ j_U:U\to Z$ satisfies $h\circ a\circ j_U=b\circ i_T\circ j_U=(b\circ j_{U'})\circ i_U$. Call $P(U')$ the set of morphisms $c:U'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ c=b\circ j_{U'}$ and $c\circ i_U=i\circ a\circ j_U$; $P(T')$ is the set of solutions of the universal property for $(T\subset T',b,a)$. (R) Let $U''\subseteq U'$ be opens of $T'$, with $k:U''\to U'$ the inclusion ($j_{U'}\circ k=j_{U''}$), $U_0=i_T^{-1}(U'')\subseteq U=i_T^{-1}(U')$ with inclusion $k_0:U_0\to U$ ($j_U\circ k_0=j_{U_0}$), and $i_{U''}:U_0\to U''$ as above. If $c\in P(U')$, then $c\circ k\in P(U'')$: $h'\circ c\circ k=b\circ j_{U'}\circ k=b\circ j_{U''}$, and $c\circ k\circ i_{U''}=c\circ i_U\circ k_0=i\circ a\circ j_U\circ k_0=i\circ a\circ j_{U_0}$, where $k\circ i_{U''}=i_U\circ k_0$ because both, composed with the open immersion $j_{U'}$, give $i_T\circ j_{U_0}$ (uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]). (A) If $U'$ is affine, $P(U')$ has exactly one element, by the previous step applied to $U\subset U'$, $b\circ j_{U'}$ and $a\circ j_U$.

proof.text: *Arbitrary $T'$: glueing.* By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] choose a covering $T'=\bigcup_{k\in K}T'_k$ by affine opens, and let $a'_k$ be the unique element of $P(T'_k)$ (previous step, (A)). For $k,l\in K$, the open $T'_{kl}=T'_k\cap T'_l$ is covered by affine opens $W'\subseteq T'_{kl}$ of $T'$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; for each such $W'$ the restrictions of $a'_k$ and $a'_l$ to $W'$ both lie in $P(W')$ by (R), hence are equal by (A). By the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] (for the scheme $T'_{kl}$ and its covering by these $W'$), $a'_k|_{T'_{kl}}=a'_l|_{T'_{kl}}$. By its existence clause there is a morphism $a':T'\to Z'$ with $a'|_{T'_k}=a'_k$ for all $k$. It lies in $P(T')$: $h'\circ a'$ and $b$ have the same restriction $h'\circ a'_k=b\circ j_{T'_k}$ to every $T'_k$, so they are equal [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]; and with $T_k=i_T^{-1}(T'_k)$, which form an open covering of $T$, $a'\circ i_T\circ j_{T_k}=a'\circ j_{T'_k}\circ i_{T_k}=a'_k\circ i_{T_k}=i\circ a\circ j_{T_k}$, so $a'\circ i_T=i\circ a$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Uniqueness: if $a''\in P(T')$, then $a''|_{T'_k}\in P(T'_k)$ by (R), so $a''|_{T'_k}=a'_k=a'|_{T'_k}$ for every $k$ by (A), and $a''=a'$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing].

source.place: More on Morphisms, proof of Lemma 04F3 (lemma-universal-thickening), third paragraph ('Given a general diagram we can choose an affine open covering T' = ⋃ T'_i ... By uniqueness we see that a'_i and a'_j agree on any affine open of T'_i ∩ T'_j. Hence the morphisms a'_i glue to a global morphism a' : T' -> Z' over X as desired'); the checks of the two conditions on a' and the global uniqueness written out by the agent

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By the second step $Z\subset Z'$, with closed immersion $i$ and $h'$, is a first order thickening over $X$ with $h'\circ i=h$, and by the previous step, for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $X$ with $T'$ an arbitrary scheme and every $a:T\to Z$ with $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$, there is exactly one $a':T'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ a'=b$ and $a'\circ i_T=i\circ a$. This is the defining property of a universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$ [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening].
